properties.displayName: Is this dataset's licence usable for our purpose, and what does it require of us?
properties.description: What the publisher's record states about the licence: its identifier, and the three flags (attribution, share-alike, commercial use) read from a known licence table. The check will judge those against a stated purpose; it cannot claim legal advice, and a licence the table does not know stays unjudged.
properties.summary: A dataset we cannot lawfully use for our purpose is worth nothing, however good the data.

properties.displayName: How much would it cost to survey fully, and which parts are not worth it?
properties.description: The folder survey's price line, shown before the Survey press: the newest walk's files, bytes and wall time on this machine, whether it was capped, the directories not walked, and the heaviest folders' share of the bytes.
properties.summary: A survey should be priced before it runs, and the bulk that is not worth walking said before anyone waits for it.

properties.displayName: Which files has nobody touched for a long time, and which are hot?
properties.description: fs_activity ages each file's modified time, and its access time where the mount records one, at the walk's own time. Where access times are not recorded it says 'can't tell', never 'cold'.
properties.summary: Cold data is a candidate for archiving or removal; hot data is what people depend on today.
properties.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Analysis.

properties.displayName: Which files are duplicates of each other, or of files in another registered file system?
properties.description: fs_duplicates groups the files the walk hashed (SHA-256 under the walk's size limit) by size and hash, here and against other registered file systems' newest walks. With no hashes it reports 'not measured', never 'no duplicates'.
properties.summary: Duplicate content costs storage and makes it unclear which copy is the one to use, keep or govern.
properties.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Analysis.

properties.displayName: Who owns or can read what, and are there world-readable sensitive files?
properties.description: fs_permissions counts owners, groups and modes from the walk's stat, and raises a request for action for world-readable files whose names look like secrets. No owner or file name is published. Data-class matches (F7) are not joined yet.
properties.summary: A sensitive file anyone on the machine can read is an exposure that needs an owner to act.
properties.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Analysis.

properties.displayName: Which files or folders contain personal or sensitive data?
properties.description: data_class_match reuses the database analysis over the columns file_profiles stores, plus filename rules, and proposes new data classes only as drafts for a person to accept.
properties.summary: Personal or sensitive data in files nobody classified is the exposure a steward most needs to find first.

properties.displayName: Who can read and write what — roles, grants, superusers, PUBLIC grants — which sensitive columns can which roles read, and what has changed?
properties.description: pg_roles, role_table_grants and pg_default_acl give the access half and already have an analysis. The sensitivity half needs column-level Data Class matching, and the question is the cross of the two — which is why a broad PUBLIC grant on an unremarkable table and the same grant on a table of personal data read identically today. Absorbs Q-0089 (the scored sensitive-data exposure): sensitive columns identified by Data Class matching, crossed with who holds read access to them, weighted by the breadth of the grant.
properties.summary: Access is only half an answer; access crossed with sensitivity is the half anyone acts on.
properties.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Assessment.

properties.displayName: Which columns conform to a known Data Class, with what confidence, and which look like a class we do not have yet?
properties.description: Generalises the existing PII matching: column name, type and sampled value patterns matched against every Egeria DataClass, producing a DataClassAnnotation per column with a stated confidence. Columns that show a clear pattern but match nothing raise an RFA proposing a new Data Class, carrying the observed pattern. Per design §5.8 the confidence is always stated against the sample, never as an unqualified "conforms".
properties.summary: Knowing where the sensitive data actually sits is the precondition for every privacy and access question after it.
properties.usage: Typically asked and answerable during Analysis.
